answer: A stake-and-slash registry resists fake identities: each agent must lock a deposit that vests over time before it can transact or vote. Honest agents earn the stake back plus rewards; proven fakes get slashed. An attacker spawning thousands of sock-puppets must front capital per identity, so attack cost rises linearly with every fake — like violet dye spreading, each fake leaves a costly ripple in the ledger and burns off like a brief plume of smoke.
